clue.text: Unsuccessful football manager took charge after international

indicators.note: the phrase for taking charge is placed after the international abbreviation

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, runs English football
led means took charge

explanation.surface: A national team's coach has flopped after taking over at international level.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA (Football Association) is English football's governing body, here cast as its manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that failed was not a success, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Mail ignoring Queen's secret affair

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to leave the queen's letter out of the armour word

parts.note: mail is chain armour worn by knights
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Royal post being skipped while a hidden romance goes on in the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail' looks like letters, but it is the medieval chain armour.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, typically an illicit or clandestine one.

clue.text: Profited from Labour supporting Liberal intellectual

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after the Liberal letter

parts.note: to have earned is to have profited from one's work

explanation.surface: A political pundit notes a Labour backer who made money from the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' with its capital suggests the UK party but here is simply work.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person is scholarly and well read, so the adjective matches intellectual.

clue.text: Member of police force becomes tense during bust

indicators.note: becomes says one letter turns into another inside the broken word

parts.note: bust means broken, faulty: defective
F is the physics abbreviation for force
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A police officer gets nervous during a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of police force' reads as one phrase, but 'force' belongs to the wordplay; 'during bust' says where the swap happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective is an officer of the police who investigates crimes.

clue.text: Deceitful character's broken promise to cut back

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged
cut back means trimmed at the back, losing the final letter

explanation.surface: A fraud breaks a pledge to reduce spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut back' trims 'to' to T, which joins PROMISE in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposter pretends to be someone else, a deceitful character by definition.

clue.text: Queueing outside entrance to Co-operative Bank

indicators.note: outside means the queueing phrase wraps round the other letter

parts.note: standing in a queue is being in line

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Customers wait in a queue at a branch of the Co-operative Bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-operative Bank is a British bank; here 'Bank' is a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of earth is a slope, and an incline is a slope too.

clue.text: Beat with stick

explanation.surface: Hitting someone with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is slang for a thrashing and also means to fix with glue.

clue.text: Get anxious about lifting top

parts.note: to sweat over something is to worry

indicators.note: lifting in a down answer turns the word for about upwards, reading it backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about raising a lid or heavy weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is a garment for the upper body, and a sweater is one example.

clue.text: Exchange article with one in supplementary reference for free

indicators.note: with completes the exchange, the other letter going back the opposite way
exchange says the article letter and the one letter trade places

parts.note: supplementary means extra
to cite is to refer to, so cite stands for a reference
A is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Swapping a word for a numeral in a footnote to set it loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange article with one': the A and the I of EXTRACITE swap places, A becoming I and I becoming A.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to release from a tangle, so it means to free.

clue.text: Passionate fellow captivated by contents of erotica

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside the other letters
contents of a word are its letters without the outer ones

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An ardent man enthralled by steamy literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic nature is ardent and emotional, close to passionate.

clue.text: Rubber silencer fitted round American gun

indicators.note: fitted round says the silencing letters go round the gun word

parts.note: sh is said to silence someone
heat is US slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A rubber cover placed over a US firearm's suppressor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silencer' suggests a gun part, but it is the word hushing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber is slang for a condom, also called a sheath.

clue.text: Copy note containing right answer with student's help

indicators.note: containing means the note word holds the others inside

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a crib is an illicit aid for a student

explanation.surface: A student copies out a message containing the right answer from a crib sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcribe is to write out a copy of something.

clue.text: Cotton on sticky part of plant

definitions.meaning: to understand suddenly, to cotton on
a stick-like part of a plant

explanation.surface: Cotton fibre on a gummy piece of plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky' here means like a stick, not gluey.
explanation.definitionFit: Twig is informal for grasp, and a twig is a small shoot or branch.

clue.text: Source arranged drugs for part of newspaper article

parts.note: the head of a river is its source
a line is a dose of cocaine laid out in a strip

explanation.surface: A newspaper source set up a drugs deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' is not an anagram signal: a line of cocaine is powder arranged in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the title printed above a newspaper story.

clue.text: Life with former partner is strained we hear

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: we hear says the next word is spelt by how it sounds

parts.note: strained means tense

explanation.surface: Living with an ex is stressful, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence is being alive, so it can stand for life.

clue.text: Raid fashionable street

parts.note: in means fashionable
a street is a road

explanation.surface: A police swoop on a trendy street.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an incursion into enemy territory, a raid.

clue.text: Impose ban on criminal tried in court

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge bans something about a criminal on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun for the defendant, but it is the anagram signal on 'tried'.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict is to forbid or prohibit by authority.

clue.text: Writer's point regularly belies little for the consumer

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A pen point that hides how small it really is for buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' is one who eats, not a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A nibble is a small bite, a little bit to eat.

clue.text: Wipe empty table at end of seat to eat

indicators.note: wipe says these letters are erased from the end of the seat word

parts.note: a banquette is an upholstered bench seat

indicators.note: empty leaves only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Clearing a table at the end of a bench before dining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at end of' says the letters removed are the last ones of BANQUETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To banquet is to feast, to eat lavishly.

clue.text: 3 could make the grade

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 3, LEARNED, in its sense of found out

indicators.note: could make says these letters may be made into something else

explanation.surface: Someone who learned enough might pass the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' stands for the answer to 3 Down, in the sense of having found something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Having gathered something is having learned or inferred it.

clue.text: Common man who's risen through the ranks

definitions.text: man who's risen through the ranks
definitions.meaning: a senior army officer, high in rank

explanation.surface: An ordinary man who has been promoted from the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: General means widespread, and a general is a top military officer.

clue.text: Passes out: asleep and beginning to snore

indicators.note: out means not in the proper state, so the letters are rearranged
beginning to gives the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone loses consciousness, dozing and starting to snore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes out' reads as fainting, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Time elapses as it passes by.

clue.text: 26 turned round in shock

indicators.note: turned round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: the answer at 26, TESTES, is slang nuts

explanation.surface: A kick in the testicles is a nasty jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze, as a shock does.

clue.text: Frolic before friend with a gloomy air

parts.note: frolic is fun
ere is an old word for before
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Playing before a friend, rather glumly.
explanation.definitionFit: Funereally means in the manner of a funeral, solemnly and gloomily.

clue.text: Thin mattress leads to night of terrible upheaval for back

indicators.note: for back means the result is read backwards
the leads to words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A poor mattress causes a night of back trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheaval' looks like the reversal signal but is fodder; 'back' turns the initials round.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a thin padded mattress of Japanese origin.

clue.text: Great act of generosity gives away odd bits to sister

indicators.note: gives away means these letters are lost from the generosity word

parts.note: largesse is generous giving

indicators.note: odd bits are the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A grand gesture that gifts some pieces to a sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Large means big or great in size.

clue.text: Introduce charge when Independent becomes accessible to everyone

indicators.note: becomes says one letter turns into another

parts.note: to indict is to charge formally with a crime
U is the film classification for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A newspaper's price drops so all can buy it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second I of INDICT is the one that changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To induct someone is to introduce them formally into a post or group.

clue.text: Put back in controls head of state ultimately sought

parts.note: reins control a horse
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the monarch

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter

explanation.surface: A head of state finally seeking to be back in control.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinsert is to put something back into place.

clue.text: Security feature present in electric blankets

indicators.note: blankets means covers, so these words cover the answer

explanation.surface: A safety cut-out built into electric blankets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blankets' looks like part of the heating appliance but signals the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard, part of a security set-up.

clue.text: Part of tennis match repeatedly knocked back balls

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters are hit back the other way, read in reverse

parts.note: repeatedly asks for the tennis piece once more, so it supplies those same letters a second time
a set is a part of a tennis match

explanation.surface: Tennis balls returned again and again during a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles SET to SETSET, and 'knocked back' reverses it. 'balls' looks like tennis balls but is slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is slang for testicles, and testes is the anatomical name for them.
